clues: This port city sits on a bay on the Sea of Japan, in the far east of Russia.
This port is oddly cold for its spot on the coast. In winter, winds blow in from the vast landmass, and the cold sea chills it more.
It began as a Russian army post in 1860. A treaty with China had just handed this coast to Russia.
This port is the end of the line for the famous Trans-Siberian train. The long ride across Russia stops here, by the sea.
This is Russia's largest port on the Pacific. It is the main hub of the Russian Far East.
